name: 2-ingredient cheese-dough stuffed rolls (לחמניות בצק גבינה ממולאות)

source.author: Instagram / blog (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: No-yeast, no-rise 2-ingredient dough (self-rising flour + a tub of white cheese/cottage/yogurt) with fresh za'atar/oregano, stuffed with mozzarella + Bulgarian cheese and pan-fried. Makes 9 rolls. Analyzed PER ROLL for the whole roll (dough + filling + absorbed frying oil). Frying oil assumed ~1.5 tbsp absorbed across the batch. White-cheese tub taken at 5%. Estimate — no macros given. User asked for improvement recommendations (see suggested_mods).

ingredients.note: or 2 cups plain flour + 1 packet baking powder; swap to whole-spelt self-rising for fiber
cottage or 5% white cheese = most protein; yogurt = lighter
very salty + brined — see her safety note; light hand recommended

steps: Mix all the dough ingredients to a smooth dough.
On a lightly floured surface form a ball and cut into 9 pieces.
Flatten each piece into a round by hand (or a rolling pin).
Place both cheeses in the center, gather the edges in and pinch to seal into a closed ball.
In a lightly oiled pan, space the balls out and flatten slightly; fry both sides until golden, flipping several times and gently pressing with a spatula.

batch_totals.note: All 9 rolls incl. filling + ~1.5 tbsp absorbed frying oil. Sodium is high (self-rising flour + salt + salty Bulgarian cheese). The frying oil and the Bulgarian cheese are the main calorie/fat/sodium levers.

him.verdict: Tasty but it's fundamentally a fried white-flour bread: per roll ~189 kcal with only ~7.5 g protein (~4 g protein per 100 kcal) and ~25 g refined carbs. The cheese dough gives it more protein than a plain roll, but the white flour means almost no fiber and the pan-frying adds oil calories on top. Fine as an occasional treat or a carb portion, not a protein anchor. The good news: it's very easy to upgrade — a few swaps roughly double the fiber and cut the added oil (see mods).
flags: ~7.5 g protein / roll, ~25 g refined carbs (~4 g protein per 100 kcal)
low fiber (~1 g) — white self-rising flour
pan-fried — added oil calories (~1.5 tbsp across the batch)
high sodium (~320 mg/roll; ~2,900 mg batch) — flour + salt + Bulgarian cheese
cheese dough does add protein + calcium vs a plain roll
suggested_mods: Swap to WHOLE-SPELT or whole-wheat self-rising flour (or plain whole flour + baking powder) — roughly doubles fiber, keeps it whole-grain
Use COTTAGE or 5% white cheese for the dough (more protein than yogurt); add a scoop of the tub's whey/an egg white if you want to push protein
BAKE instead of fry: brush with egg + sesame and bake 190–200 °C ~18–22 min — cuts the added oil almost entirely for a similar golden crust
Go light on the Bulgarian cheese (biggest sodium lever) — 30 g Bulgarian + 70 g mozzarella keeps flavor with less salt; skip the ¼ tsp added salt
Boost protein-per-roll in the filling: mix in some low-fat white cheese or a little grated 9% yellow cheese with the mozzarella
Serve with a salad/tomato to add the fiber + vitamin C the roll lacks; the fresh za'atar is a great keep (flavor + antioxidants)

her_preconception.verdict: A calcium- and protein-contributing cheese bread that's fully cooked, so it's broadly fine — with one thing to check. The Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese: it carries a Listeria note in pregnancy unless pasteurized. Pan-frying heats it through (cooked cheese is considered safe), and most Israeli 'Bulgarit' is pasteurized anyway — just verify it, or lean on mozzarella instead. Otherwise the white cheese/cottage/yogurt and mozzarella are pasteurized and fine. It's not a big prenatal-nutrient source on its own (white flour); the whole-grain swap adds folate + iron.
prenatal_highlights: calcium + protein from the cheese dough + filling
whole-grain flour swap would add folate + iron

safety_advisories.note: Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's cooked here (fried through) which is considered safe, and most Israeli Bulgarit is pasteurized; verify or use more mozzarella instead.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized, cook through (as here), or use pasteurized mozzarella/hard cheese

suggested_mods: Verify the Bulgarian cheese is pasteurized, or shift the filling toward mozzarella
Use whole-grain self-rising flour for folate + iron; pair with veg for a rounder meal

cooking_guide: Mix the dough JUST until it comes together and is smooth — don't overwork it. A cheese + self-rising dough turns tough and dense if over-kneaded; stop as soon as it's uniform.
Rest the dough 10 min under a towel so the flour hydrates and it's easier to shape.
Divide into 9 even pieces. Flatten each into a round ~½ cm thick, a little thinner at the edges so the seal isn't too thick.
Put the mozzarella + Bulgarian in the center, don't overfill (cheese leaks if you do), gather the edges up over the filling and pinch firmly to seal into a closed ball. Set seam-side DOWN.
Heat a lightly oiled or nonstick pan over MEDIUM-LOW. Place the balls seam-down, spaced apart, and flatten slightly into thick discs.

Cover the pan — this steams the thick center so the dough cooks through before the outside burns. Fry, flipping several times and gently pressing with a spatula, until deep golden on both sides and cooked in the middle (5–8 min total).
If any cheese escapes and crisps in the pan, that's a bonus — scoop it onto the roll. Serve hot while the cheese is melty.

LOWER-OIL OPTION: instead of frying, set the sealed balls on parchment, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame, and bake at 190–200 °C for 18–22 min until golden — nearly the same result with almost no added oil.
Tip: fresh za'atar or oregano in the dough is worth keeping; a little grated garlic or chili flakes in the filling lifts it too.
